shots.vo: They told you *"no"* twelve times. Would you quit?
Edinburgh, the nineties. You are a single mom living on benefits. You write a book in a café *while your daughter sleeps* in her stroller.
You send the manuscript to publishers. The first "no". The second. *The fifth*.
Twelve publishers say no. At home — *an empty fridge* and bills.
You could give up. Get a normal job. *And forget it*.
But you send it once more. The head of a small publisher takes a chapter home to his eight-year-old daughter Alice. She finishes it and asks: *give me more*.
The first print run — just *five hundred* books. Today more than *six hundred million* have been sold. This is J. K. Rowling and "Harry Potter".
